title: Number to Roman Numeral

concept.title: Greedy with a table that includes the subtractive forms
body: Write the largest symbol that still fits, subtract its value, and repeat. This works when the table also contains the six subtractive pairs, in descending order of value: 1000 M, 900 CM, 500 D, 400 CD, 100 C, 90 XC, 50 L, 40 XL, 10 X, 9 IX, 5 V, 4 IV, 1 I.
Because 900 and 400 and the others are in the table, you never have to think about "IIII" or "VIIII": the largest piece that fits is always taken first.

statement: Convert a number from 1 to 3999 to a Roman numeral. Use the symbols I=1, V=5, X=10, L=50, C=100, D=500, M=1000 and the subtractive forms IV=4, IX=9, XL=40, XC=90, CD=400, CM=900.
hints: List the values from big to small, including 900, 400, 90, 40, 9 and 4.
For each value, write its text as many times as it fits.
Subtract the value each time you write its text.

explanation: Take the biggest value in the table that still fits, write its text, subtract, and repeat.
solution.complexity: Time O(1) (at most 15 symbols), space O(1).

code.python:
n = int(input())

table = [(1000, "M"), (900, "CM"), (500, "D"), (400, "CD"), (100, "C"), (90, "XC"),
         (50, "L"), (40, "XL"), (10, "X"), (9, "IX"), (5, "V"), (4, "IV"), (1, "I")]
out = ""
for value, text in table:
    while n >= value:
        out += text
        n -= value
print(out)
